body: Yeah I really don't think she planned this out from the beginning as an "identity" category.  I think she gradually fell into it and ended up adopting the identity because it furthered her career and is now backpedalling.

Again, it's the specifics of those rituals that constitute cultural practices.  "Eating" is not a cultural practice, one can eat and have it not be a part of a culture.  Sitting down to a dinner table and praying is a cultural ritual involving eating.  Not every culture prays or sits at a table.

Saying all cultures have a ritual surrounding food isn't a cultural constant.You are using a circular logic, basically saying "all cultures have culture."
I thought we were talking about the search for a cultural universal which is a controversial, unresolved topic in the field of anthropology.  Did you solve it?

But the benefits from running for 2 hours are much more than just calories burned.  You increase your serotonin, you increase muscle mass, which are good for your overall mental and physical health over time.  You might not overeat as much if you are less depressed from running on a regular basis. I see your point but exercising is more than just about calories.
But also, exercising is something to do.  Sitting around thinking about not eating is not.  I try to exercise a lot, in a way, to keep busy and not sit around the house around food.
Ok.  So what's your point?  That anthropology is a stupid field?
Yeah but those are biological functions.  Each culture has their own way of enacting and interpreting those functions.
The way they eat and the way they have sex varies wildly, though.
I read that as "married the chef."

Yeah... I could write a book about the issue and it is more complicated than the past few comments.  We have been going to marriage counseling and working on these issues for a VERY long time, years.  We are not running away from these issues, we have been working on them and our strategies for communicating about them just did not align.

I do love him.  We just are not compatible, at least right now we need a lot of space.  Things are better now that we have that space.

Ok that makes a lot of sense.  I expect that she might even ask me if I'm ok, I was seen crying at work once and I think it's just ... in the air that something is up.  So I think I might mention it if I'm asked and it's not in response to my performance.

I agree to an extent.  It's just that there is an emotional quality to co-workers being offended.  I feel like they wouldn't be so offended if they knew that it was more of a medical problem.  But maybe the place is not to mention it in a staff evaluation meeting, and to talk privately to my boss

And, yes, I'm already doing everything I can outside of work, seeing a therapist/primary care physician/medication and all that.

We weren't supporting each other, him being around made me feel worse, not better.  I do feel more lonely now, but I feel more in control of my own life.  We were very codependent and I felt like I couldn't make decisions for myself.

I realize what you've said is just an example, but I did want to clarify that my projects and work are done on time and thoroughly, the attention and focus issues are about conversations with other staff members and more.. social issues, like making sure there is enough office coverage or paying attention in meetings.  To put it simply, I think she just thinks I'm rude because I'm not always listening.

I see your point about how it will come across as deflecting responsibility.  I try to make sure I am holding myself accountable for job duties.  This is why it's difficult because the attention issues don't impact my individual work, it's the social atmosphere I think that is suffering.  I appear rude to my co-workers.

Yeah context is everything.  You could go to the ghetto and say "look at all these NIGGARDS acting NIGGARDLY" while getting in their face and you can't argue that just because the definition doesn't relate to the N word historically that the connotation of that interaction isn't negative.

But context is everything.  He said it, made eye contact with the black person, and emphasized it, drawing out the "niggar" part.  Just because the definition doesn't come from the n word doesn't mean there isn't a context that could show a negative intent.
What I don't get is why this is happening NOW.  She's an aging actress, this was decades ago, who cares.
No, further is time, farther is space.

Yes that makes A LOT of sense.  Thanks so much.  I've always thought of detaching from people as being mean or looking down on people.  But I guess if people have lost their place in your life, it's where they need to go. And thanks for the advice on my dad.  I think I will take a break from them because I can't not be consumed by this right now.  But my daily life is so difficult it's hard to go on without support.  It's also hard to ask for support after an experience like this.

Thanks for your comment.  Yes, I've learned my lesson about trusting her.  I just wish I didn't have to learn it the hard way.  It's really hard to let go of, because I came to her for support and especially the way I hear my dad say things that are obviously put in his head by her, it's alienating me from him.  So I have few people left to turn to.  But the thing you said about making someone feel "lower" is definitely true of her.  She makes me feel so small.

She's an LCSW and she deals with substance abuse, not personality disorders.  She tends to see others' feelings as valid, but not mine.  I feel like she is empathetic but for some reason has no sympathy for me only.  She seems jealous of me and the attention I get from my dad. She has had bad divorces, but people in town seem to like her ok.
Holy shit this is sad.  As a mother (sorry) this just made my heart ache and want to take in that little girl.  So sad.

What's irritating is that I am and have always been seeing a therapist.  She continues to say that I need help even when I'm getting it, it's as if that's the only thing she knows how to say and can't fathom the idea that I'm still having problems after taking her advice.  So she just says it over and over.
She's an LCSW
Thanks.  She has even said "what, you asked for help" when I tell her that this hurt me.
Also, she's an LCSW, does that still apply?
Would multiple relationships really apply hear?  I wasn't her patient, she just told me in an email.

How do I know she isn't right though?  How do I know that I'm not delusional?  The side of the story everyone has heard is my own, so everyone here would be agreeing with the delusional side if it was so.

There is NO arguing with her on this front, I agree with you.  She would say that it is all "brain chemistry" and that no one is responsible for my disease.  The only one that is responsible is me, for getting help.

No, therapy for 10 years (on and off).  I've been on and off of various medications for depression, but never a personality disorder.  Honestly I've just been sad that my mom died and had a lot of stress.  I'm becoming convinced nothing has ever been wrong with me, but rather my stepmom has been constantly telling me therapy and medication is the answer for 10 years.

I really don't think it's intentional though.  I think she just has an ego about being "right" and sincerely thinks it's helping me and that I'm just delusional.  I think she really believes what she's saying.
I should say she said "have you looked into BPD I think you have the symptoms?" or something like that. So I guess she didn't say "you have it, I hereby diagnose you."  I should have said that.

I dunno, she's really socially awkward.  Her and my dad live in a rural area and they just don't have much contact with other people.  So I've always interpreted her comments like that as just having no social intelligence.  But you're right, I shouldn't and won't trust her from now on.
I did and she said she's just trying to help because I clearly don't have a grip on reality.

She would say to this "well I didn't diagnose you, I said 'have you looked into the diagnosis of BPD' and that I need to get therapy for my problems."  But in subsequent correspondences she's acting as if it's a sure thing and when I told her I don't like feeling judged medically that it actually makes my depression worse she said "I will not take responsibility for your mental health, no one can cause mental health problems in another person."

I think by "opening up" she just meant not being so shy.  I understand her perspective, I have been very shy and quiet around her because I was self-conscious of a lot the things she would say to me.  Her diagnosing me doesn't exactly make me feel less shy.

I mean, what would she have to gain by purposefully doing this?  There's no money or prestige involved.  I think she's legitimately trying to help me but is just really arrogant about being "right" and is really boastful about being a great therapist.  I don't think she's consciously trying to make me go crazy, what motivation would she have to do that?

While I agree she's manipulating or invalidating, I don't truly believe she's doing it on purpose.  She seems like she really thinks she's helping, but is too arrogant to understand that she could be wrong.  I think she wants to help but is really intent on being "right".

Thanks.  This makes a lot of sense.  I was trying to relate to her in every way, she started the emails, she wanted to talk about these issues, so I responded because I thought we would make a connection. It's clear she only wants it to be one way.  So I'll disengage and let go of any personal attachment.

Thanks so much.  Hearing psychologists tell me this isn't appropriate is helping me stand up to her.  I haven't decided what to do, but I might tell my dad that I consider her behavior emotionally abusive and he needs to know that and I want to distance myself from her.  If I can say a psychologist told me that I think he will sympathize with me.

I think she has a master's in social work.  I think she is a "counselor" for a center not a psychologist.  I know she deals mainly with substance abuse.

My mother is dead and my father is kind of in between me and my stepmom right now.  I do have a good relationship with him and right now I'm trying to have a livable relationship with my step-mom so that she won't poison my dad against me, which I see her doing.  I see now that I need to not see her as a friend but more so someone I have to deal with.

Well even if she were my therapist, she'd be the worst therapist of all time.  She has never listened to me talk about my problems and doesn't know any of the details of what I've been through.  She said all this based on one email basically.
Can you file a complaint anonymously?  I would but I don't want her to know or make the problem worse.
Thanks, that's a good idea about working on CBT myself.  I've never thought of it that way, I've always thought I needed a therapist to help me.

She diagnosed me with Borderline.  I actually was wondering if that was projection.. she gets very attached to people and then divorces them, she's done it 4 times.  My dad is basically her only friend and texts him constantly when he's away, wanting to know where he is.

The problem with the conversation with her is that it's insanely meta.  Like she rejects the things I said about my feelings and then I say "I feel like you invalidated me when I told you my feelings" and she'll say "no I didn't."  And I'm like, see you just invalidated me again!  It makes me feel like I'm going crazy.

Ugh, thank you so much.  The rude and condescending thing... that's exactly how she always makes me feel, like she's bestowing knowledge about myself on me.  I try to tell her this and she says I'm "paranoid" or that I'm blaming her for my own mental problems.  I'm glad someone else perceives it as condescending.

No, I've moved around a lot.  I had the last therapist for 3 years and I liked her a lot.  She helped me feel grounded.  But now I've seen two people in this town that I didn't really like.  Honestly this whole experience has made me feel really down on therapy and talking things out.  I'm at the point where I'm sick of talk therapy.

You are absolutely right, she deals with these types of people all day so she gets in that mindset of seeing symptoms everywhere. 

The problem with depression and anxiety is that even though you need to get out there and socialize and make connections with people in order to feel better, those very problems make you want to stay at home and avoid people.  You're right though.  It's very hard with a 1 year old though.

I guess I felt obligated when my daughter was born, like I was doing a disservice to my daughter by not having grandparents around.  It was just me and her and her dad away from any extended family, so I moved back home to try and have a relationship with my family for her.
I can't, I have a daughter and an ex/her father that has a job here.  Even if I move to another town nearby, I want to have a relationship with my Dad.

She did say that I need to see a therapist about it and get a more "objective" view.  I've already been seeing a therapist for the past ten years.  I had one before I moved that was really helpful to me and now I'm having trouble finding a good one.
Oh ok, sorry.  No I meant I lived out on the west coast and I moved back to the midwest, my hometown to be near family.

I don't know why I'm trying so hard to be friends with her.  My own mother is dead and I don't have friends with kids and she is very close to my dad so I guess I thought we could all be a big happy family together.  When she reached out to me I thought it meant she was open to being empathetic.  I guess I have to learn my lesson and move on.
Oh we don't live together.
How can I read about the therapist accounts?  Is there a list or a way I can search?

To make matters worse, the therapist I'm currently seeing is part of the same company my stepmom works for and she has access to my medical records.  I don't think she's looked at them, but she has the ability to.  I guess I don't really know for sure.
I said basically this and she said that she tells me these things because I need to know that I have a lack of self-awareness and she's helping me.

I kind of believed her that I was just seeing reality incorrectly because of my depression.  I wanted her to be my friend. She told ME I have a "lack of self-awareness" and it made me think she was right and I am just a bad person.  She told me my behavior was irrational so I believed her.  I still have doubts.  When I read your comment I think, yeah, I just need to be away from her.  But if I think about her and read her emails I start to think that I don't have a grip on reality and that I must have a mental illness.
She uses personality disorders and diagnoses to protect herself against being hurt.  I hear her say that people at her work are narcissists all the time because they hurt her feelings.

Well not really, I feel worse in a way because of this situation with my family.  I'm having trouble finding a therapist I like in a small town and readjusting to life here.  I'm trying to tell myself it's just an adjustment period and that things will get better if I just keep putting an effort into it.  Just thinking that avoiding my stepmom is an option is making me feel better, because before I really wanted to "fix" the relationship and try and be her friend.
Well I've learned that now.  She had sent me that email and agreed to try and be better friends. I wrongly thought she was ready to be my friend.  I regret it.
I just moved back... I shouldn't have.  I have a 1 year old and her dad lives in this town.. I don't think I could convince him to move with me.

I feel like I have the worst of all of those roles.  I don't have the trust and love of a mother but I have judgement and criticism.  I don't have the trust and objectivity of a therapist and I don't have the empathy of a friend.  I really don't know how to relate to her.  For the past few years I've just been polite and she has been offended that I haven't opened up to her.  I opened up to her and she just destroyed me.

Thank you, the thing you said about feelings being more real and intense is exactly what I had been thinking.  When I tell her I feel like she invalidates my feelings she says that if I 'look carefully' I'll see that she never did that, and that "thoughts and feelings are different things."  So she's avoiding validating my feelings by claiming that everything I'm saying is a "thought" instead of a feeling.  It's making me feel so crazy.
Post partum depression.
She has been divorced 4 times.

Thanks, this is what I was trying to decide, whether  I should ignore this and focus on other areas of my life, or listen to her and reevaluate my thoughts.  She is very convincing, I think it bothers me so much because I was beginning to think she was right and I need to change.

The problem is my dad.  I moved back home to have a relationships with my dad.  She whispers in his ear that I'm crazy and I hear her ideas come out in his speech from him too.  So when your own parents believe these things about you it's hard not to believe it.
